To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the future of PLM is a Closed Loop Product Life Cycle Management, based on a new definition of Intelligent Product and on a new definition for product data.
1) The product data technologies for closed loop PLM are not mature enough to support a seamless exchange of dynamic product data.
1) The current product lifecycle management standards are not sufficient for the management of the product data of future generations of Intelligent products.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new generation of product data technology standards and architectures, based on semantic technologies, to allow the seamless interoperability, sharing, and re-use of data, knowledge, and information along the whole product lifecycle, from design to end-of-life.

the following topics: - Definition of the concept of intelligent products and the associated product data technologies (PDT), - Definition of a closed loop product data management (C LPDM) approach, - Definition and development of a closed loop PLM architecture, - Identification and analysis of the requirements of the different stakeholders, - Definition and analysis of the different levels of intelligence of intelligent products, - Definition of a reference architecture and the corresponding reference model of intelligent products, and - Definition of an integrated PDT framework.
the definition and development of the next generation Product Data Technologies for the management of the product lifecycle data of intelligent products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art in PDT and PLM is far from being able to support the vision of intelligent products and their lifecycle.
the current situation is not satisfactory.
the current standards and technologies are not able to cover the requirements of the emerging intelligent products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the actual standards for PDT do not allow the seamless interoperability for Intelligent Products.
the actual state of PDT standards is not sufficient for the management of future intelligent products.
the current state of the art in Product Data Technology is not yet sufficient to support the Closed Loop PLM of Intelligent Products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need a new paradigm of product data management and exchange which is based on a new concept of intelligent products, which is based on the concept of closed loop product lifecycle management.

the current standards for PDT do not cover the whole product lifecycle, but only a part of the product lifecycle and that there is a need for new standards for PDT covering the whole lifecycle of products and product systems, including the management of dynamic data, and for the seamless integration of the different PDTs.

the future of PLM will be based on the integration of the PLCS with the Internet of Things (IoT) and the Internet of Services (IoS) in a Closed Loop PLM environment, where the PLCS will be extended to the management of the product's life cycle and the PLCS will provide a framework for the integration of the IoT and IoS.
